# Faultline

> An on-call agent whose brain is a per-tenant FalkorDB operational context graph. Rule: "no path, no claim". It
> blames a change only when FalkorDB returns a causal path from the change to the symptom (`algo.SPpaths`) and shows
> the change can carry the observed impact (`algo.maxFlow`); otherwise it abstains and hands the incident to a human.
> It then proposes the smallest containment (max-flow min-cut, each option tried on a `GRAPH.COPY`), routes to who
> should fix it (`algo.HarmonicCentrality`, escalation by `algo.MSF`), pages the on-call, takes one human-approved
> action (a real pull request), verifies it through a second channel (APPLIED / NOT_APPLIED / UNKNOWN) and writes the
> decision back into the same graph. Built for Graph Hacks (WeMakeDevs × FalkorDB); tracks T1 (Agents That Act on
> Connected Data), T3 (Company Brain), T2 (Agent Memory & Coordination). Every number below is checked against
> evals/results/latest.json by `make claims` (the HTML comments are those checks).

## Try it

- Live demo (keyless, simulated GitHub): https://13-203-185-119.sslip.io
- Hosted read-only MCP server, public demo key: docs/MCP.md (`https://13-203-185-119.sslip.io/mcp`)
- Narrated video (4:25): docs/media/demo.mp4 and the GitHub release asset
- Give any MCP client the graph tools: `npx -y @prashantthakur77/faultline-mcp` (npm; connects to the live demo, `--url`/`--key` for your own server)
- Run the whole product with Docker only: `curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prashant-thakur77/Faultline/main/deploy/quickstart.yml && docker compose -f quickstart.yml up`, then http://localhost:3000
- Reproduce everything offline with no API key: `make setup && make judge-check` (prints PASS)

## What it proves (measured, with 95 % intervals in docs/PROOF.md)

- Safety: <!-- claim:seedsall.deep.wrong_confident -->0<!-- /claim --> confident wrong blames in <!-- claim:seedsall.deep.cases -->1540<!-- /claim --> adversarial generated worlds; a telemetry heuristic blamed an innocent change in <!-- claim:seedsall.deep.T.wrong_any -->620<!-- /claim --> of them, and a strong LLM alone (claude-opus-5-5) in <!-- claim:llm_deep.deep.all.wrong_confident -->37<!-- /claim --> of <!-- claim:deep.fresh.all.cases -->140<!-- /claim -->.
- The trade: Faultline names the right cause in <!-- claim:deep.fresh.all.right_cause -->51<!-- /claim --> of <!-- claim:deep.fresh.all.cause_cases -->100<!-- /claim --> headline worlds and abstains on the rest; the LLM names <!-- claim:llm_deep.deep.all.right_cause -->66<!-- /claim -->, the heuristic <!-- claim:deep.fresh.all.T.right_strict -->85<!-- /claim -->. It trades recall for never blaming the wrong change.
- The graph is load-bearing: where the look-alike has its own fault, the right cause in <!-- claim:decisive.full.g5_only.right_cause -->20<!-- /claim -->/<!-- claim:decisive.full.g5_only.cases -->20<!-- /claim --> worlds with `algo.maxFlow` and <!-- claim:decisive.no_maxflow.g5_only.right_cause -->0<!-- /claim --> without it; with FalkorDB off, <!-- claim:arm.A4.confirmed_causes -->0<!-- /claim --> causes are confirmed (it fails closed).
- A real system (FaultBench-OTel, the OpenTelemetry Demo with its own fault flags and real telemetry; topology and decoys ours): the right cause in <!-- claim:otel.faultline.right_cause.k -->11<!-- /claim --> of <!-- claim:otel.faultline.right_cause.n -->20<!-- /claim --> faults, <!-- claim:otel.faultline.wrong.k -->0<!-- /claim --> wrong blames in <!-- claim:otel.faultline.wrong.n -->40<!-- /claim --> windows; a telemetry threshold was wrong <!-- claim:otel.Tplus.wrong.k -->8<!-- /claim --> times.
- On call: a scripted night passes <!-- claim:oncall.night.steps_passed -->14<!-- /claim -->/<!-- claim:oncall.night.steps -->14<!-- /claim --> steps; the repeat fault is fixed under a standing approval with <!-- claim:oncall.night.inc2.people_woken -->0<!-- /claim --> people paged; the contract fires in <!-- claim:oncall.night.negatives_fired -->0<!-- /claim --> of <!-- claim:oncall.night.negatives -->5<!-- /claim --> cases outside its terms.
- Learning (T2): the fix the on-call keeps choosing moves up the next plan; the memory and coordination checklist (track T2) is <!-- claim:t2.green -->5<!-- /claim -->/<!-- claim:t2.items -->5<!-- /claim --> green.
- FalkorDB at scale: <!-- claim:tenants.n -->250<!-- /claim --> tenant graphs on one engine with <!-- claim:tenants.acl.leaks -->0<!-- /claim --> leaks in <!-- claim:tenants.acl.cross.n -->1000<!-- /claim --> cross-tenant reads; at <!-- claim:scale.10k.services -->10000<!-- /claim --> services the proof path's engine p99 is <!-- claim:scale.10k.tail.Q-GATE-1.engine_ms_p99 -->8.926<!-- /claim --> ms; all 10 `algo.*` against NetworkX: same answers on <!-- claim:algo10k.same -->9<!-- /claim --> of <!-- claim:algo10k.comparable -->11<!-- /claim -->, engine faster on <!-- claim:algo10k.faster_engine -->11<!-- /claim --> of <!-- claim:algo10k.timed_pairs -->12<!-- /claim -->.
- Honest limits: FalkorDB's own GraphRAG-SDK beat the company brain on blind questions, <!-- claim:graphrag.s2.sdk.correct -->32<!-- /claim --> against <!-- claim:graphrag.s2.fl.correct -->24<!-- /claim --> of <!-- claim:graphrag.s2.questions -->40<!-- /claim -->; most worlds are synthetic; see docs/HONEST_LIMITS.md.
- Live, measured from outside over HTTPS: the hero incident right and verified APPLIED <!-- claim:live.hero.applied -->5<!-- /claim --> of <!-- claim:live.hero.n -->5<!-- /claim --> times.

## How it uses FalkorDB

- One graph per tenant, read-only ACL users, `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` with a timeout and a row limit for every read; writes only through one module.
- <!-- claim:repo.algorithms -->10<!-- /claim --> `algo.*` procedures, each changing a decision (BFS, SPpaths, SSpaths, maxFlow, pageRank, betweenness, WCC, labelPropagation, HarmonicCentrality, MSF).
- <!-- claim:repo.templates -->233<!-- /claim --> parameterised Cypher templates (never Cypher built from input), <!-- claim:repo.mcp_tools -->60<!-- /claim --> MCP tools, <!-- claim:repo.constraints -->18<!-- /claim --> constraints, vectors (`vecf32`) and full-text indexes, `GRAPH.COPY` clean rooms, `WAITAOF` durability, the engine's telemetry stream.

## Docs

- README.md: the full write-up (how it works, graph model, query catalogue, results, safety, limits)
- docs/PROOF.md: every number with its N, interval and kind
- docs/EVALS.md and evals/PREREGISTRATION.md: methods and pre-registration
- docs/GRAPH_MODEL.md, docs/QUERY_CATALOGUE.md, docs/FALKORDB_COMPAT.md: the graph, its queries, the pinned engine
- docs/HONEST_LIMITS.md: what is synthetic, what did not work
- docs/upstream/: what was reported to FalkorDB
